t: There are authorized to be appropriated for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2022 such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act, to be derived from amounts appropriated in each such fiscal year for the operation of the Architect of the Capitol, except that the aggregate amount appropriated to carry out this Act for all such fiscal years may not exceed $40,000.

fable.w: This section only authorizes appropriations, drawn from Architect of the Capitol funds, and caps the total at $40,000. There is no tempting reading here: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. The Architect of the Capitol is itself a federal entity, so nothing crosses the federal boundary.
fable.s: There are authorized to be appropriated for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2022 such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act

qwen_chat.w: This section is a standard appropriation clause authorizing the expenditure of funds. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government. The mention of the Architect of the Capitol refers to the source of the funds, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: There are authorized to be appropriated for each of fiscal years 2017 through 2022 such sums as may be necessary to carry out this Act, to be derived from amounts appropriated in each such fiscal year for the operation of the Architect of the Capitol, except that the aggregate amount appropriated to carry out this Act for all such fiscal years may not exceed $40,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for the "Architect of the Capitol," which serves Congress, there is some form of participation. However, this section is purely an appropriation clause. It does not describe any process of consultation, coordination, or decision-making involving outside parties. It simply authorizes the spending of money.
